data.reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed both PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO, finding standard Python packaging from official PyPI with pinned sha256sums and no malicious indicators. The qwen model's inconclusive verdict resulted from an API error (HTTP 400), not a security concern, and its initial audit also found no dangerous top-level code. Both models identified the same source (files.pythonhosted.org) with proper checksum verification, standard build/package functions using python -m build and python -m installer, and no .install hooks or patches.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from a tool failure rather than substantive analysis differences. The qwen model encountered an LLM API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) during full PKGBUILD review, forcing an inconclusive verdict despite its initial audit finding the file safe. The deepseek model completed its review successfully and found no issues.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to complete PKGBUILD review due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: API errors during file review should not produce inconclusive verdicts when initial audits succeed - implement fallback to initial audit results when full review fails
When multiple models review the same package and one fails due to tool errors, the successful model's verdict should carry decisive weight if it covered all relevant files
Distinguish between 'inconclusive due to analysis uncertainty' and 'inconclusive due to tool failure' in verdict reporting
